nodes.label: Log a Mock Primary CTA
nodes.rationale: The only filled terracotta button in the chrome, with a plus icon, placed at the bottom of the nav groups: recording an attempt is the product's single primary action and stays a deliberate, one-place gesture.

nodes.label: Metric Strip (4-cell overview)
nodes.rationale: Renders as one divided hairline-ruled strip of four overview cells rather than individual cards; shown here as four skeleton cells while analytics load. Each cell is the link to the surface that acts on its metric.

nodes.label: Performance Preview Panel
nodes.rationale: Dashboard teaser for the analytical workspace: icon, serif 'Performance' title, 'How your recent results are moving. The full analysis lives on its own page.', a 'View performance' link button, and skeleton chart placeholders. The full evidence stack stays on /performance; the dashboard only previews it.

nodes.label: Personal Tasks Card
nodes.rationale: Owns the selected day's personal work: terracotta check icon, 'Your own work for the selected day.' subtitle, an 'All tasks' switch, a task-progress bar (shown loading at 0%), the dated heading '23 Nov', the quick-add row and a 'Loading your todos...' state. Personal tasks are deliberately separate records from plan assignments.

nodes.label: Quick-Add Todo Input
nodes.rationale: Dated inline composer ('Add a todo for 23 Nov') beside an 'Ungrouped' group dropdown and a + Add button; helper copy: 'Press Enter to add. Open a task to add notes, priority, or subtasks.' — quick add creates, the task surface enriches.

nodes.label: What's the Plan! (Plan Overview)
nodes.rationale: Editorial section head grammar: small-caps dateline 'PLAN OVERVIEW' + serif title 'What's the Plan!' + one hairline rule. It hosts the two-column plan workspace (Today's Plan panel left, Personal tasks card right) and owns the plan position.

nodes.label: Workspace Header
nodes.rationale: Carries the sidebar toggle, the WORKSPACE > Dashboard breadcrumb, Search (Ctrl K) and the theme toggle — and deliberately no account identity, which lives in the sidebar footer.

nodes.label: Dashboard Loading State Screenshot
nodes.rationale: Reference screenshot of the authenticated /dashboard route captured in its skeleton loading state (1280x1136, 2026-11-23 data visible). Documents the dashboard reference layout: left paper sidebar with STUDY PLANNER / RESULTS nav groups, terracotta Log a mock CTA, identity footer and active-exam note; header with breadcrumb, Search Ctrl K and theme toggle; a 4-cell metric strip; the PLAN OVERVIEW 'What's the Plan!' section with Today's Plan + Personal tasks two-column workspace; a skeleton strip row; and a Performance preview panel. Serves as the layout reference the responsive system must keep pixel-stable on desktop.

nodes.label: Paper/Ink/Terracotta Design Language
nodes.rationale: House style evidenced across the frame: warm paper surfaces, ink text, terracotta accent reserved for primary action and active state, serif headings ('What's the Plan!', 'Personal tasks', 'Performance'), small-caps datelines (PLAN OVERVIEW, STUDY PLANNER, RESULTS), thin hairline rules, square corners, no shadows.

nodes.label: Skeleton Loading State Mirroring Route Geometry
nodes.norm_label: skeleton loading state mirroring route geometry
nodes.rationale: Design pattern: the loading state mirrors the route's real geometry — muted beige placeholder blocks shaped like the metric cells, plan panels, calendar cards and charts — never a bare spinner, so layout does not jump when data arrives. Copy states the pending operation ('Loading task progress... 0%', 'Loading your todos...').

nodes.label: Workspace Sidebar
nodes.rationale: Design intent: the paper sidebar owns everything that must survive a route change and that the header must not carry — grouped navigation, the single primary CTA, utility destinations, and account identity (avatar, name 'Local Developer', email dev@localhost, sign-out icon). Identity is deliberately kept out of the header, which only holds trigger, breadcrumb, search and theme toggle.

nodes.label: --accent collision (brand color vs neutral hover)
nodes.rationale: shadcn primitives expect a neutral hover accent, but here --accent is the brand color; compensate via tokens or wrappers, never blind forks.

nodes.label: Fixed chart subject hues (per-subject identity)
nodes.rationale: Series colors are fixed per subject and identical in every palette so switching palettes never re-colors data.

nodes.label: shadcn semantic token bridge (:root aliases)
nodes.rationale: Aliases are defined only in :root so .dark resolves them through var() chains to palette tokens rather than redeclaring.

nodes.label: Six brand palettes (data-palette)
nodes.rationale: Each palette is an identity redeclaring 10 neutrals plus accent for light and dark; status colors and chart hues stay shared so data never re-colors.

nodes.label: OKLCH token system (six data-theme palettes)
nodes.rationale: The full shadcn variable set in OKLCH for six palettes with graphite default; agents use Tailwind semantic classes only and never edit globals.css.

nodes.norm_label: token map: six brand colors to shadcn semantics

nodes.label: Empty Examination Hall
nodes.rationale: Rows of wooden desk-and-chair units recede toward the horizon in muted gray-beige wash on warm paper; they are the quiet scaffolding that makes the single occupant legible — an exam room mid-session, not a classroom.

nodes.label: Lone Candidate Figure
nodes.rationale: The only human presence: a figure seen from behind in a white shirt, seated at the composition's center among the desks. Design intent — the aspirant faces the hall alone, mirroring the self-driven, single-account practice the tracker records.

nodes.label: Red Seal Stamp
nodes.rationale: Vermilion artist's seal in the top-right corner follows the East Asian ink-painting chop convention, signing the artwork and balancing the warm-paper field. The seal's characters are decorative and not reliably legible — uncertain reading, treat as AMBIGUOUS.

nodes.label: Stack of Study Books
nodes.rationale: Four thick hardbound volumes (cream page blocks, maroon/red covers) stacked at the desk's left edge, beside the writing sheets. They ground the scene in preparation and study material — the syllabus load behind every mock — and, with the disc, balance the figure on the right half of the frame.

nodes.label: Terracotta Sun Disc
nodes.rationale: A large flat salmon-terracotta circle rising behind the book stack on the left — read as a rising sun motif (uncertain whether sun or moon is intended, but the flat-disc reading is clear). It is the image's one saturated color and matches the house accent, which stays terracotta in every palette and is never repurposed, tying the illustration to the site's token system.

nodes.label: Student Writing at Desk
nodes.rationale: The composition's single human figure: a boy with dark hair in a white collared school shirt, seated on a wooden chair at a wooden desk, right hand driving a black pen across loose sheets while his left hand steadies the paper, gaze fixed downward. Design intent — an aspirant mid-practice, doing the exact act (writing a paper) whose results the tracker records, shown with quiet focus rather than celebration.

nodes.label: Ink Hall Illustration
nodes.rationale: Landing ink art asset (1024x1024 PNG): a watercolor-and-ink scene of one candidate seated alone among rows of empty desks in a silent examination hall, giving the anonymous-only landing a quiet, editorial image of solitary exam preparation rendered in the site's warm paper-and-ink language.

nodes.label: Ink Hero Student Illustration
nodes.rationale: Landing ink art asset (1152x864 PNG, 4:3): a watercolor-and-ink illustration of a young aspirant in a white short-sleeved school shirt seated at a wooden desk, head bowed in concentration, writing on loose exam papers with a black pen, a stack of four thick books and a large flat terracotta disc at the desk's left edge on a plain warm-paper field. Filename indicates hero placement for the public landing, rendered in the site's paper-and-ink editorial language. Added together with the five sibling ink assets (ink-books, ink-compass, ink-hall, ink-lantern, ink-trend) in commit 04a11d8 'port the prototype's chat bubbles and landing ambience'; grep of HEAD shows no live component referencing /landing/ink-hero-student.png (the landing Plate art in the refine-two-style-ui worktree uses ink-compass.png), so at HEAD it is a parked landing-art asset kept in public/landing/.

nodes.label: Ink Wash Aesthetic
nodes.rationale: Soft watercolor/ink rendering in warm paper and muted ink tones matches the landing's editorial paper-and-ink design language (consistent with the landing's ink art island and tone-inverted ink-plate treatment), so the illustration reads as part of the house style rather than a pasted photograph.

nodes.label: Negative Space Composition
nodes.rationale: The upper two thirds of the frame are deliberately blank warm paper: the empty field gives editorial serif headlines room above the art, keeps the illustration subordinate to landing copy, and matches the house design language (warm paper surfaces, thin rules, serif headings, no shadows).

nodes.label: Solo Aspirant Metaphor
nodes.rationale: One candidate among many empty seats makes the product's one-person framing visible without UI chrome: a private workspace that records one aspirant's mocks — exactly what the anonymous-only landing introduces before sign-in.

nodes.label: Aspirant Practice Metaphor
nodes.rationale: One student, one desk, one paper being written: the image literalizes the product's subject — deliberate, self-driven practice recorded attempt by attempt — making the tracker's promise visible to an anonymous visitor before sign-in. The empty upper-left field keeps room for editorial serif headline copy, subordinating the art to the landing's copy-first hero grammar.

nodes.label: Ink Wash Aesthetic
nodes.rationale: Fine ink linework over soft watercolor washes on a warm-paper field, in the same hand as the five sibling ink assets, matching the house design language (warm paper surfaces, thin rules, serif headings, no shadows). The illustration therefore reads as part of the landing's editorial artwork family rather than a pasted photograph or stock render.

nodes.rationale: L1 is a free per-instance token bucket, L2 the cross-instance authority; AI holds a dedicated 20/min budget in both so it never contends with writes, and degrading never means allowing.

nodes.label: otp-input.tsx boxed 6-digit input
nodes.rationale: One real transparent input under six cells keeps SMS autofill, paste-splitting and one accessibility field all working.

nodes.label: Neon Auth invariants
nodes.rationale: No app-owned user rows, no writes to neon_auth, no server-side owner reassignment; a different account is always a separate workspace.

nodes.label: Verified-ownership invariant
nodes.rationale: Ownership is always the verified Neon Auth user ID; accepting userId from a body, query or backup would let one account read or write another's records.

nodes.label: Server-side email auth gates (Neon console)
nodes.rationale: Flows only succeed when the Neon Auth project enables them service-side; a disabled method answers 404 and every surface says so honestly.

nodes.label: Shared read services (src/lib/services/*)
nodes.rationale: Pages and their /api handlers call the same read services so scope, ownership and trash filtering cannot drift between the two paths.

nodes.label: Colocation rule (route/_segment/ to shared/)
nodes.rationale: A route's components stay private beside it until a second route imports one, then it moves to src/components/shared/; enforced by tests/colocation.test.ts.

nodes.label: Folder-routing architecture (2026-11-20)
nodes.rationale: Every route is a real Server Component page that authenticates and prefetches its own data; the old single client orchestrator was deleted on purpose.

nodes.label: Zustand ui-store (global UI state only)
nodes.rationale: Only ephemeral UI state lives in Zustand; server data belongs to the query cache and durable preferences to their own homes.

nodes.label: Ask AI Workspace Page (/ask)
nodes.rationale: Dedicated full-page /ask conversation surface, captured in its final hairline pass. Header row pairs a sparkles glyph square with the serif 'Ask AI' title, 'New conversation', and a read-only info badge; 'New chat' (pencil) and 'Hide history' (history icon) actions sit on the right. The page is shown in its unconfigured state: the center panel hosts the 'Set up your AI provider' card while 'Loading AI settings…'. A small emoji-style sticker sits bottom-right (purpose uncertain - decorative easter egg).

nodes.label: Conversation Rail
nodes.rationale: Left column of the /ask page: a 'Search chats' input with a compose (new chat) icon button, the 'No chats yet' empty state, and the read-only usage footer pinned at the bottom ('Read-only - the coach answers from your workspace').

nodes.label: Hairline Design Pass
nodes.rationale: The screenshot series this image belongs to documents the final 'hairline' design iteration - warm paper surfaces, square corners, thin rules, serif headings, no shadows; the 'final-ask' filename marks this as the settled /ask layout for that pass.

nodes.label: Log a Mock Sidebar CTA
nodes.rationale: The only filled pill in the navigation - the primary 'Log a mock' action is visually promoted above every nav link, keeping the tracker's core write path one click away even from read-only AI pages.

nodes.label: No Chats Yet Empty State
nodes.rationale: Empty conversation history renders a quiet 'No chats yet' line inside the rail rather than a blank column, sharing the empty-state grammar used by both AI surfaces.

nodes.label: Set Up Your AI Provider Card
nodes.norm_label: set up your ai provider card
nodes.rationale: The unconfigured-AI state of the /ask center panel: 'Ask AI runs on your own provider key. It is encrypted before storage and never returned to this page.' with 'Loading AI settings…' beneath - the entry state of the AI settings form before any provider is configured.

nodes.label: Read Ledger Panel
nodes.rationale: Right column titled 'THE READ LEDGER' - a timeline of real AI usage rows (shown as 'Loading activity…' here) captioned with the info note 'Read-only - the ledger records reads, never writes', so the privacy promise is visible exactly where usage evidence is read.

nodes.label: Workspace Sidebar Navigation
nodes.rationale: sscinsight. / MOCK WORKSPACE wordmark over two grouped navigation sections - STUDY PLANNER (Dashboard, Study calendar, Today's plan, My tasks) and RESULTS (Mock history, Compare mocks, Performance) - with Settings and Trash icons and the Local Developer (developer@localhost) account block in the footer rail; visible here as the persistent chrome around the /ask page.

nodes.label: Bring Your Own Provider Key
nodes.rationale: Per-user AI credential design principle stated by the setup card copy: the user supplies their own provider/model/key, the key is encrypted server-side before storage, and it is never returned to the page - users verify the trust model in product copy rather than in settings help text.

nodes.label: AI Read-Only Pledge
nodes.rationale: Design intent: AI never writes - the coach answers from the user's data only. The pledge is restated three times on this single screen (header 'Read-only' info badge, usage footer 'Read-only - the coach answers from your…', ledger caption 'the ledger records reads, never writes') so the promise survives any glance position; it mirrors the implementation guarantee that AI routes never call repository writes.

nodes.label: Ask Three-Column Measured Grid
nodes.rationale: Layout decision visible in the screenshot: a measured three-column grid (narrow conversation rail, flexible center conversation column, narrow read-ledger column at lg) so the full-page /ask mirrors the ~520px AI sheet grammar instead of forking a second transcript design, while giving the usage ledger a stable right margin; below lg the ledger collapses into a bottom drawer.

nodes.label: TargetReference comparability
nodes.rationale: A target is drawn only against the tier it was set for; mixed-maxima views are marked incomparable instead of drawn as one misleading line.

nodes.label: Catalog versioning with attempt snapshots
nodes.rationale: Numbers cite the official notice; a correction is a new CATALOG_VERSION while saved attempts keep their snapshot, so history is never rewritten.

nodes.label: Tier pattern snapshotting on save
nodes.rationale: Each tier's pattern comes from the official notice and is recorded on the attempt at save, so a later catalog correction never changes a past result.

nodes.label: Dashboard Loading State (Mid-Load Frame)
nodes.rationale: Captured on 24 Nov while server data was still streaming: every data region (metric strip, plan chart, task progress) shows skeleton geometry, while the navigation chrome is fully rendered and interactive - the deliberate pattern that loading states preserve real page geometry.

nodes.label: Log a Mock Primary CTA
nodes.rationale: The single dark filled pill button ('+ Log a mock') sits at the bottom of the sidebar nav - the only high-contrast filled element in the chrome, making the core tracking action the loudest affordance while everything else stays quiet hairline ink-on-paper.

nodes.label: Metric Strip Loading Skeleton
nodes.rationale: The overview strip renders as ONE divided band of four cells separated by vertical hairline rules (not individual cards); during load each cell shows placeholder geometry (label pill, large value blob, sub-line) so the real layout geometry is preserved - loading mirrors the page's true shape, never a bare spinner.

nodes.label: Next.js Dev Overlay Artifacts
nodes.rationale: Dev-mode capture artifacts, not product UI: a red 'N 1 Issue' badge (Next.js dev overlay issue count, bottom-left) and a round palm-tree badge (bottom-right; dev-tools indicator or sticker - AMBIGUOUS reading). Their presence dates the capture to a dev server session.

nodes.label: Personal Tasks Card
nodes.rationale: Card titled 'Personal tasks' with a check-square icon, subtitle 'Your own work for the selected day.', a shuffle/random action and an 'All tasks' filter pill in the header; body shows 'Loading task progress... 0%' above the selected date '24 Nov' - confirming personal tasks are scoped to the selected calendar day and surface a progress percentage while loading.

nodes.label: Plan Overview Editorial Section Head
nodes.rationale: Editorial head grammar: small-caps dateline 'PLAN OVERVIEW' above a large serif display title 'What's the Plan!', set under a full-width hairline rule. Beneath it sits one large empty chart placeholder (suspected the radar/outcome ring mid-load - exact chart identity is an AMBIGUOUS reading).

nodes.label: Sidebar Study Planner & Results Nav Groups
nodes.norm_label: sidebar study planner & results nav groups
nodes.rationale: Navigation is grouped under small-caps section labels: STUDY PLANNER (Dashboard, Study calendar, Today's plan, My tasks) and RESULTS (Mock history, Compare mocks, Performance), with 'Dashboard' shown as the active item in a filled paper-on-ink pill. Mirrors the workspace route map (dashboard, calendar, plan, my-tasks, history, compare, performance).

nodes.label: Workspace Shell Chrome (Sidebar + Header)
nodes.rationale: Reference frame for the final hairline pass of the persistent chrome: a paper sidebar with a serif 'sscinsight.' wordmark over a 'MOCK WORKSPACE' subtitle (reading of the double-c in the wordmark is uncertain), grouped navigation, a utility footer (Settings, Trash, user identity 'Local Developer / developer@localhost' with an LD avatar), and a header carrying a sidebar-collapse icon, 'WORKSPACE > Dashboard' breadcrumb, a Search pill with 'Ctrl K' hint, and a sun-icon theme toggle. No shadows anywhere - structure is carried by thin rules and tone.

nodes.label: Hairline Design Language
nodes.rationale: The 'hairline-final' filename marks this as the approved end-state of the hairline design pass: warm paper surfaces, square corners, thin hairline rules and dividers instead of shadows, serif display headings with small-caps datelines, quiet ink-on-paper chrome, and exactly one filled dark primary CTA. Every structural boundary in the frame is a 1px rule, not elevation.

nodes.label: Latest Result Section
nodes.rationale: Trails the plan stack with the most recent mock result; in this capture it renders '—' above 'Results unavailable', keeping the section shape while its data source is unreachable.

nodes.label: Next.js Dev Overlay Issues Badge (2 Issues)
nodes.norm_label: next.js dev overlay issues badge (2 issues)
nodes.rationale: Incidental tooling artifact, not product UI: the red 'N · 2 Issues ✕' pill bottom-left is the Next.js dev-mode overlay indicator reporting two dev-time issues during capture.

nodes.norm_label: personal overdue metric (nothing overdue in my tasks)
nodes.rationale: Renders a computed zero with a friendly empty-state message ('0 — Nothing overdue in My Tasks') rather than an error, showing overdue count as a headline metric inside the plan stack.

nodes.label: Sidebar Navigation: Study Planner + Results Groups
nodes.norm_label: sidebar navigation: study planner + results groups
nodes.rationale: Paper sidebar holds two small-caps nav groups — STUDY PLANNER (Dashboard, Study calendar, Today's plan, My tasks) and RESULTS (Mock history, Compare, Performance) — with Settings + Trash as footer utilities and the signed-in account block ('Local Devel… dev@localhost', a local dev session) at the bottom; labels truncate with ellipsis at the 15rem width, and the group dateline sits beside a hairline rule.

nodes.label: Today's Plan Dashboard Section
nodes.rationale: Leads the dashboard content stack; in this capture it renders its unavailable state — an em-dash placeholder, a 'Plan unavailable' line, a checked 'Plan completed' stat line, and a second 'Plan unavailable' line — so the day's schedule degrades without blanking the section.

nodes.label: Workspace Header: Breadcrumb, Search, Theme Toggle
nodes.norm_label: workspace header: breadcrumb, search, theme toggle
nodes.rationale: A single hairline-ruled header bar carries the 'WORKSPACE › Dashboard' breadcrumb, a 'Search Ctrl K' affordance, an unnamed (empty) slot, and a circular sun-glyph theme toggle; no account identity lives here.

nodes.label: Graceful Degraded-State Pattern (em-dash + 'unavailable' labels)
nodes.rationale: Design intent visible in the capture: a data outage must degrade, never blank or crash — each section keeps its geometry and names what is missing ('Plan unavailable', 'Results unavailable'), unknown values render the neutral em-dash '—' rather than an invented number or zero, and a genuinely computed empty value (overdue = 0) still states itself with a friendly message. A data outage degrades to the section's normal unavailable state, never a 500-style wall.

nodes.label: Hairline Rule Aesthetic
nodes.rationale: The capture demonstrates the house 'hairline' language the filename references: warm paper surface, square corners, 1px thin rules separating header, sidebar groups and content sections, serif-leaning type, no shadows and no heavy cards — structure is drawn with rules, not boxes.

nodes.label: attemptSchemaFor(pattern)
nodes.rationale: The single write/import validation contract so form entry and backup import cannot duplicate or diverge layout rules.

nodes.label: Browser Connection Error Page
nodes.rationale: Chromium's standard network-failure page ('This site can't be reached') with suggestion links 'Checking the connection' and 'Checking the proxy and the firewall', a Details button, and a Reload button.

nodes.label: ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED
nodes.rationale: Chromium network error code meaning the TCP connection was actively refused - here the local Next.js dev server was not running when the screenshot was taken.

nodes.label: Localhost 127.0.0.1 Dev Server
nodes.rationale: The refused host is the loopback address where the app's local dev server listens; its absence caused the failed capture.

nodes.label: Dashboard Final Screenshot
nodes.rationale: The filename marks this as the intended final dashboard design reference, but the actual captured frame is a Chromium 'This site can't be reached' error page: the local dev server at 127.0.0.1 was not running at capture time, so no dashboard UI was recorded. Flag for review: replace with a real dashboard capture before using this file as a design reference.

nodes.label: Ink Wash Illustration Style
nodes.rationale: Loose grey ink-wash clouds, warm cream paper, black-spined hardcovers and exactly one saturated accent (the red ribbon) keep the illustration inside the landing's warm-paper/ink editorial grammar; the single red accent mirrors the design system's one-hue accent discipline (terracotta) rather than introducing a new palette.

nodes.label: Landing Ink Art
nodes.rationale: Named client island of the editorial landing page that mounts ink illustrations; this PNG in public/landing/ is one of its assets, alternating with paper sections to carry the paper-and-ink mood of the product.

nodes.label: Study Time Discipline
nodes.rationale: A twin-bell alarm clock resting on a five-book stack with a red ribbon bookmark reads as exam preparation under time pressure: the clock (deadline, timed mocks) sits literally on the books (study material). This is the motive behind using the art on the SSC Insight landing — a mock tracker where every attempt carries an IST date and a 50-day plan counts down study time.

nodes.label: AES-256-GCM credential encryption
nodes.rationale: Personal keys encrypt under AI_CREDENTIAL_SECRET and plaintext never leaves the server; rotating the secret degrades rows to not-configured instead of erroring.

nodes.label: AI subsystem (read-only, fail-closed)
nodes.rationale: AI is optional, server-only and never writes; every output is a draft the user explicitly applies, and it fails closed when unconfigured.

nodes.label: AI context whitelist
nodes.rationale: Only aggregates, subject/section stats, target and the latest 20 full mocks are sent; notes, identity and per-attempt detail never leave the server.

nodes.label: Prompt sanitization and tag-forging defense
nodes.rationale: Control/bidi/zero-width characters are stripped and JSON data blocks escape angle brackets so a stored value can never forge a delimiter or system message.

nodes.norm_label: ssrf guard with pre-call dns re-check
nodes.rationale: Base URLs are user-controlled, so loopback, RFC1918, metadata and reserved ranges are blocked and DNS is re-resolved immediately before every provider fetch.

nodes.norm_label: endpoint safety (ssrf guard, dns rebinding residual)

nodes.label: Planner restore always-merge rule
nodes.rationale: Leaving planner work out of exports silently dropped completions; restore therefore never regresses a completion and replace deletes mocks only.

nodes.label: updatePersonalTask status-enum rule
nodes.rationale: Sending a derived boolean collapsed in-progress tasks and ran the reopen cascade that cleared every subtask tick.

nodes.label: Vercel request-body constraint (4MB import cap)
nodes.rationale: Vercel request bodies are about 4.5MB, so the import transport cap is 4MB; the limit is environmental, not a product rule.

nodes.norm_label: portable json backup (no identity or credentials)

nodes.label: Import merge/replace with safety download
nodes.rationale: Replace is the only deliberate immediate destruction in the product, which is why the safety backup download and account-name confirmation are mandatory.

nodes.label: Three independent target systems
nodes.rationale: Percentile goals, structure-keyed marks defaults and per-tier overrides answer different questions; conflating them produces meaningless comparisons.

nodes.label: Single /api/exams settings cache
nodes.rationale: A write updating scope but not targets (or vice versa) is exactly how a target could silently disagree with its own maximum.

nodes.label: Aspirant's Journey Metaphor
nodes.rationale: The plate dramatizes the product's promise with a solitary lamp-lit scholar climbing endless stone steps toward a flag: daily incremental effort (stairs), guidance through the dark (the single warm lantern accent against the monochrome wash), and the exam-selection goal (summit flag). The one warm color against gray ink keeps the aspirant's hope as the only lit element, matching the landing's paper-and-ink editorial language.

nodes.label: Gray Brush Baseline Wash
nodes.rationale: Broad, dry horizontal gray-brush strokes run along the lower third beneath the curve like a ruled baseline or ground wash, anchoring the rising line and echoing the landing's thin-rule, paper-first aesthetic.

nodes.label: Mid-course Dip and Plateau
nodes.rationale: Midway along the stroke it crests, dips and wobbles through a short plateau before the steep final climb - progress is deliberately drawn as non-linear, with a visible setback between early gains and the late surge rather than a smooth monotonic line.

nodes.label: Red Endpoint Accent Dot
nodes.rationale: A small solid vermilion circle sits at the stroke's tip, the only saturated color besides the ink. It reads as the latest data point - a 'you are here' marker ending the trend - and echoes the landing's terracotta accent and the red seal marks shared across the ink-art family.

nodes.label: Rising Brush Trend Line
nodes.rationale: A single continuous black brush stroke climbs from the lower-left corner to the upper right, tapering from a thick anchored start to a fine tip - the picture's entire subject is a score curve going up. The calligraphic taper gives the rise momentum, the way the product's trend charts draw toward the target.

nodes.label: Ink Trend Brush Illustration
nodes.rationale: Landing ink art asset (1344x768 PNG): one hand-drawn dry-brush line rising from lower left to upper right with a mid-course dip, a solid red dot at its tip, and broad gray brush strokes as a baseline, all on warm textured paper. Editorial artwork in the site's warm paper/ink language. Note: no reference to this file was found anywhere in src at extraction time - it is presumably part of the landing's 'ink art' family described in CLAUDE.md (ink-books, ink-compass, ink-hall, ink-hero-student, ink-lantern siblings live beside it) but is currently unwired in code; flagged AMBIGUOUS against the landing composition.

nodes.label: Compass Direction Motif
nodes.rationale: The brass pocket compass with its star rose stands for guided preparation: the tracker points an aspirant's study in a fixed direction (dated plan, targets) instead of wandering. It is the landing's navigation/direction metaphor rendered as a physical object.

nodes.label: Landing Ink Illustration Style
nodes.rationale: Paper-background ink-and-watercolor spot illustration with loose washes, thin ink outlines, soft cast shadows and red seal marks - matching the landing's warm paper/ink editorial design system. One of the ink-* artwork family in public/landing/ (ink-books, ink-hall, ink-hero-student, ink-lantern, ink-trend) used by the landing's 'ink art' islands.

nodes.label: Scroll and Handwritten Ledger Motif
nodes.rationale: A rolled paper scroll beside an unrolled sheet of handwritten lines (text itself illegible squiggle, not read) stands for the recorded mock-attempt ledger - work written down, dated, and kept. The handwriting is decorative, not content.

nodes.label: Red Wax Seal Stamp Motif
nodes.rationale: The glossy red seal stamp (with small red seal marks in the artwork's corners) evokes official certification - results, ranks and notices stamped as authentic - and echoes the landing's terracotta/red accent on an otherwise ink-and-paper palette.

nodes.label: Dry-brush Ink Medium
nodes.rationale: Dry-brush ink on textured warm paper: visible bristle streaks in the stroke and the grainy gray wash keep the chart metaphor hand-made rather than computational, matching the house editorial style (warm paper surfaces, serif headings, thin rules, no shadows) and the ink-art family's shared medium.

nodes.label: Landing Ink Illustration Style
nodes.rationale: One of the landing's ink-* artwork family in public/landing/ (siblings ink-books, ink-compass, ink-hall, ink-hero-student, ink-lantern), sharing the paper-background ink-and-watercolor editorial language with red accent marks; the ink-compass extraction's style rationale explicitly names ink-trend as a family member. CLAUDE.md assigns the family to the landing's 'ink art' islands, but no live code reference to this file was found at extraction time.

nodes.label: Score Progress Metaphor
nodes.rationale: The artwork is a hand-drawn score trend: overall upward movement with one dip, a marked latest point, and a flat baseline - the tracker's core story (mock scores trending toward target across attempts) rendered as editorial art instead of a chart widget.
